newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam proposes sweeping cabinet changes--source.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam proposes sweeping cabinet changes--source.

text.p: Vietnam's Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has proposed dropping more than 10 ministers and senior officials from his cabinet as part of a sweeping reshuffle, an informed government source said on Wednesday.
The source said delegates to the assembly had been presented with a list of names of people to be replaced, and would vote on this and a list of nominees for the vacant positions later on Wednesday.
Among those being dropped are Vietnam's Finance Minister Ho Te, Minister for Planning and Investment Do Quoc Sam, and head of the powerful Interior (police) Ministry Bui Thien Ngo, the source said.

Also included on the list of those on the way out are Culture and Information Minister Tran Hoan, Le Xuan Trinh of the Government Office and Nguyen Ky Cam, head of the Committee for Anti-Corruption and Smuggling.
Under Vietnam's political system their successors are unlikely to be formally appointed before the current session of the National Assembly draws to a close in about a a week.
Vietnam's cabinet comprises more than 30 people including ministers, heads of state commissions and other government bodies.
